rocky-mountain.overview: Rocky Mountain National Park has alpine day hiking, with trails climbing past glacier-carved lakes to high tundra ridges. Hikers drive or take a shuttle to trailheads like Bear Lake, where steep routes push above the treeline to sweeping views of the Continental Divide. A timed-entry reservation is usually required in the main summer and early fall season.

months.5: Lower elevation trails clear of snow, offering good hiking through the valleys. The high alpine routes remain snowbound.
months.10: Winter weather returns to the high country, closing the alpine trails to standard hiking. Lower valley trails remain walkable.

months.6: Summer conditions settle in and the full trail network is open. The Skyline Trail offers clear views over the gulf, though hikers should prepare for occasional rain and early-season insects.
months.7: The hiking season hits its peak with warm, clear days perfect for the Cabot Trail routes and the Skyline Trail.
months.8: Warm weather continues, making this an ideal time for coastal walks and highland loops.
months.9: Crisp air and clear skies provide excellent walking conditions. The coastal views are sharp, and the highland trails remain fully accessible.
months.10: Fall colors transform the Cape Breton canyons into a brilliant display of red and gold. The weather quickly cools toward the end of the month.
